history.summary: Freehold 2BR in Lorong 7 Geylang at a low $1247 PSF and an oversized 1066sqft, but the technical score flatters it: only 16 URA transactions, a 78-unit boutique block, and Geylang red-light-district adjacency all undercut exit liquidity and broad-buyer appeal. Freehold tenure is the one genuine positive.
history.rating_rationale: The headline freehold tenure and below-median PSF ($1247 vs $1581) are real, but this is a thin, niche asset for an investment hold. Just 16 URA transactions (vs 100+ for peers) means the 6.23% CAGR is statistically weak and the exit market is shallow; a 78-unit development has no liquidity cushion. Lorong 7 Geylang carries persistent vice/stigma that deters family and expat tenants and caps resale to a narrow value-buyer segment. The 1066sqft 2BR is oversized for the bracket, raising quantum without a premium-buyer to absorb it.
red_flags: Only 16 URA transactions — thin liquidity and low-confidence appreciation data
78-unit boutique development with no liquidity cushion
Geylang red-light-district adjacency (vice, crime, late-night disturbance) is a persistent stigma that narrows the buyer/tenant pool
catalysts: Freehold tenure (no lease decay) in an RCR-adjacent district
Paya Lebar Central / airbase-relocation transformation could lift D14 over the long run

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Yield optically high (~5%) on cheap PSF, but tenant quality and demand are constrained by the Geylang location; expect transient/lower-end tenancy rather than stable expat demand.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: 6.23% CAGR rests on only 16 transactions — treat as indicative, not reliable. Freehold limits downside but the location stigma caps premium re-rating.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: Discounted from thin 16-txn URA sample toward FH-boutique norm given location stigma
